field: detailedAnalysis[0].content[2] (Which Flat Roof Membrane Handles Ponding Water Best?)
quote: spray polyurethane foam loses its coating to erosion under chronic ponding, which is why the SPFA requires positive drainage on every foam roof, per the SPFA.
issue: The positive-drainage REQUIREMENT is mis-attributed to SPFA alone. facts-materials-economics.md line 372 (SPF 'Key facts / failure modes' cell) reads '...coating erosion under ponding; NRCA requires positive drainage' with sources listed as 'SPFA; NRCA' — the pack explicitly assigns the 'requires positive drainage' verb to NRCA, not SPFA. SPFA covers the coating-erosion / 30-year / failure-mode facts; the drainage mandate is NRCA's (corroborated by facts-components-specialty.md line 253: 'Low-slope/flat roofs need positive drainage — NRCA min design slope ¼ in per foot', sourced NRCA;ARMA). The author's own GAPS note (best-roofing-for-flat-roofs.md line 66) even records 'SPF positive-drainage requirement — SPFA/NRCA (§6)', so naming only SPFA contradicts both the pack and the build's own gap ledger.
fix: Keep the SPF coating-erosion fact (SPFA) but re-attribute the drainage requirement to NRCA. Before: '...loses its coating to erosion under chronic ponding, which is why the SPFA requires positive drainage on every foam roof, per the SPFA.' After: '...loses its coating to erosion under chronic ponding, which is why NRCA requires positive drainage on every foam roof, per the SPFA and NRCA.'
refuteReason: Survives refutation: verified directly against facts-materials-economics.md line 372 — the SPF cell sources are 'SPFA; NRCA' and the clause 'NRCA requires positive drainage' names NRCA as the verb's agent; SPFA backs the coating-erosion fact, not the mandate. facts-components-specialty.md line 253 independently sources the positive-drainage rule to NRCA/ARMA. The object's 'per the SPFA' alone is a genuine source-attribution error, not a defensible paraphrase.

field: commercialSection.content[0] and content[1] (Which Flat Roof Fits a Commercial Building?)
quote: TPO's reflective surface cuts peak cooling demand 11–27% per the EPA ... where the EPA's 11–27% peak-cooling-demand reduction applies to air-conditioned buildings, per the EPA and CRRC.
issue: The only pack source for the 11–27% figure scopes it precisely to RESIDENTIAL stock, and no pack supplies an EPA commercial-building cooling figure. facts-energy-solar.md line 265 reads 'reduce PEAK cooling demand by 11–27% in air-conditioned RESIDENTIAL buildings (this is PEAK demand, NOT an annual bill %)', sourced EPA, and §0.3 (lines 72–74) repeats 'the only defensible quantified cooling figure is EPA\'s reduce peak cooling demand by 11–27% in air-conditioned residential buildings'. The commercialSection (a section titled 'Which Flat Roof Fits a Commercial Building?') applies the residential-cohort number directly to commercial buildings and asserts the EPA's reduction 'applies to air-conditioned buildings' in that commercial context, extending the named source's stated cohort. The peak-demand (vs annual-bill) framing is correctly preserved, so this is a scope-broadening attribution defect, not a fabricated metric.
fix: Do not delete the figure; tighten its scope to the CRRC-rated reflectance lever rather than asserting EPA measured it on commercial stock. Before (content[0]): 'TPO\'s reflective surface cuts peak cooling demand 11–27% per the EPA' After: 'TPO\'s reflective surface carries the cool-roof reflectance the EPA credits with cutting peak cooling demand 11–27% in air-conditioned buildings.' And keep content[1]'s figure attached to the reflectance lever (CRRC-rated) rather than asserting the EPA measured the reduction on commercial buildings specifically.
refuteReason: Survives refutation: verified against facts-energy-solar.md line 265 AND §0.3 lines 72–74 — both explicitly scope the 11–27% to 'air-conditioned RESIDENTIAL buildings', and no assigned pack contains an EPA commercial cooling figure. The verdict/detailedAnalysis uses ('air-conditioned buildings', generic) are tolerable, but the commercialSection asserting the EPA reduction 'applies to air-conditioned buildings' inside an explicitly commercial-building section broadens the named source's measured cohort beyond what the pack states — a real, narrowly-scoped over-attribution.
